chunk_findings.detail: `with_no_claim` only adds a `claim` when the no-claim condition is true; it never clears an existing `claim`. If it is called on a lane that already has a claim (e.g. a cached lane view, or any caller that reuses `Lane` objects from a previous `with_no_claim`/`build` call), a later call where `probe` finds a live pid, or where `cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases` is emptied, still returns the old claim. For example, passing `Lane(..., state=S.STOPPED, claim="no claim made: old")` with `probe=lambda item: True` returns a lane whose `claim` remains set, even though the docstring says a live pid means a claim is made.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: For a bug/lesson/decision/rule expectation, `_check_other` decides existence only from `rid in table`. The work-item path explicitly treats a tombstone (`it.removed`) as `MISSING`, but the other-kind path does not inspect the table entry. Given a folded state where a deleted bug remains in `st.bugs` as a removed record (the same kind of tombstone the code already handles for `st.items`), a manifest record `{"id": "b1", "kind": "bug"}` returns `Verdict("b1", OK)`. The live bug is missing, yet `Result.all_ok` is true and the caller can report success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:_check_other

chunk_findings.detail: `expectations` iterates `ids` and `tags` directly, so a bare string is treated as an iterable of characters rather than a single id or tag. Given `expectations("A1")`, the function returns expectations for ids `"A"` and `"1"`, not for `"A1"`. If the state contains live items `"A"` and `"1"`, `check` returns all `OK` and `Result.all_ok` is true even though the intended id `"A1"` is missing. The same problem occurs for `tags="wave:1"`, which becomes six one-character tag expectations.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:expectations

chunk_findings.detail: `parse` does not validate that `kind` is a string. A manifest record with `kind = ["bug"]` (valid TOML/JSON array syntax) passes parsing, then `check` executes `if kind in _OTHER_TABLES:`. Because a list is unhashable, this raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of the intended `ManifestError`/exit-2 manifest failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: The command parameter help explicitly says `ids` may be “comma separated in one string, or a list,” but `_call` never splits commas: `ids=[ids] if isinstance(ids, str) else list(ids)`. Given an MCP call with `ids="A,B"` (or a CLI call with one positional argument `"A,B"`), the command is invoked with `ids=["A,B"]`, so the state is checked for one record id containing a comma instead of two ids `A` and `B`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/verify_filed.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: The documented TOML manifest example uses a top-level `[[record]]` table array, while the same help says a JSON manifest is “an object with `defaults` and `records`” and that an unknown manifest field exits 2. A user who creates the TOML manifest exactly as shown has a top-level key `record`, not `records`. If the parser follows the documented `records` key, this manifest contains zero expected records, so `ddflow verify-filed --manifest ...` can exit 0 vacuously (“every record is OK”) even though none of the claimed ids were checked; if it treats `record` as unknown instead, the documented example itself exits 2. Either way the documented manifest format is wrong and can produce a false OK or a spurious refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:19

chunk_findings.detail: The `SEG-inflight-registry` record has a non-empty `needs` list (`needs = ["RC-tree-result-cache"]`) but carries `tags = ["wave:0", "segments"]`. Under the stated expectation formula and rule `r-task-phase-needs-wave`, a task’s wave tag must be `1 + highest wave among its needs`; with any non-negative wave on the prerequisite, the expected tag is at least `wave:1`. For example, if `RC-tree-result-cache` is filed as a task with `wave:0`, this manifest expects `SEG-inflight-registry` with `wave:0`, so a correctly filed `wave:1` record would be reported WRONG, while a filed `wave:0` record would be accepted despite violating the wave rule.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/verify-filed-manifest.toml:29-30

chunk_findings.detail: The new line `lane = replace(lane, claim="")` clears the lane’s claim **before** `_claims_background(st, lane, cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases)` is called. `_claims_background` is the probe that decides whether a stopped lane’s claim claims background work, and it receives both the lane and the configured phrases, so clearing the claim first removes the text it needs to inspect. For example, given a stopped lane with `claim="background work still running"`, `cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases=["background"]`, and no live pid/growing output, the intended result is `claim="no claim made: ..."`. With this change, `_claims_background` sees an empty claim and returns no hit, so `with_no_claim` emits `claim=""` instead of the required no-claim status. The stale-claim fix should compute `hit` from the original lane and clear only when `hit` is false (or clear after the probe), not before it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: Given a manifest file that exists and parses successfully but contains no expectation records (for example, an empty TOML/JSON manifest), `verify_filed` returns exit 0. The argument check only sees that `manifest` is a non-empty string, `VF.load` can return an empty expectation list, `VF.check` then produces a vacuously all-OK verdict, and `res.all_ok` is true, so the function returns `O.ok`. The documented exit vocabulary says exit 2 when “nothing was asked,” and an empty manifest asks nothing; the API does not guard `if not exps` after loading.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/verify_filed.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: The `filed_max_records` knob documents that a manifest longer than the configured cap is refused with exit 3, but the stated contract for this change is that a `verify-filed` run that cannot be performed exits 2. For example, with the default cap of 500 and a manifest containing 501 records, a caller following the intended exit-code contract expects exit 2 for “could not run”; this documented exit 3 either violates that contract or makes the knob documentation wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/verify.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: The `no_claim_phrases` knob documents that a stopped lane is shown as `no claim made` unless the live-run registry holds a live pid for its item, but the change’s intent and the linked orphan-wait behavior say a growing output file also establishes a claim. For a lane whose summary says “background still running”, with no live pid but a growing output file, this documented rule says it should still be shown as `no claim made`, while the feature should treat the growing output file as evidence that work is still running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/verify.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance says a stopped lane that claims background work is running should be treated as having made a claim if either a live pid or a growing output file is recorded, but `with_no_claim` only suppresses the “no claim made” message when `probe(lane.item)` returns true, and the docstring explicitly says a growing output file is not probed. Given a stopped lane whose session summary says “running in background” and whose item has a recorded growing output file but no live pid, `probe` returns false, so the code sets `claim` to `no claim made: ... but no live process is recorded ...`, which is wrong for the required growing-output-file case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: When the expectation names a non-work kind, `check` only looks in that kind’s own table via `_check_other`; it does not apply the cross-kind wrong-kind fallback used for work-item expectations. Given a state where `st.items = {}`, `st.bugs = {}`, and `st.lessons = {"X": ...}`, and the expectation `{"id": "X", "kind": "bug"}`, `_check_other` finds no `X` in `st.bugs` and returns `MISSING`, not `WRONG` with `Mismatch("kind", "bug", "lesson")`. The module’s own work-item branch treats an id present in another table as a kind mismatch, and the docstring says a record of another kind than expected is WRONG with expected/found, so this misnames the gap and can make a coordinator believe the bug was never filed when a lesson with that id exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: `_call` does not implement the documented comma-separated `ids` form. The `ids` Param help says ids may be “comma separated in one string, or a list”, but line 18 wraps a string in a list (`[ids]`) and passes a CLI list through unchanged. Thus `ddflow verify-filed t1,t2` (one positional token) or an MCP call with `ids="t1,t2"` reaches `verify_filed` as `["t1,t2"]`, so the check treats the whole string as one id; a report that filed `t1` and `t2` is not verified correctly (it can report a bogus MISSING and exit 1, and the record count is wrong).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/verify_filed.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: The added driver text states an agent that stops waiting on background work made no claim “unless a live pid is recorded”, but the intended behavior (and the orphan-wait tie) also counts a growing output file as a live claim. An agent with a growing output file but no live pid will follow this doc and conclude no claim was made even though `ddflow lanes` is supposed to show a claim, causing the coordinator to ignore real background filing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md:270

chunk_findings.detail: The help text says the end-of-run report and `ddflow complete` “do not yet quote this output; quote it by hand until that follow-up lands.” The stated intent requires the coordinator driver doc, the agent end-of-run report (`DX-agent-final-report-rounds`), and `ddflow complete` for filing work to quote the check. Given a filing task where a background script failed to write an expected id, `ddflow complete` can still complete and report “filed” without running or quoting the state-backed `verify-filed` output, so the falsifier (“a missing id reported OK”) can still pass end-to-end despite this change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:47

chunk_findings.detail: The no-claim rule is documented as “unless the live-run registry holds a live pid for its item,” but the intent says a claim is made unless a live pid **or growing output file** is recorded. Given an agent that stops with background work whose output file is still growing but has no recorded live pid, this documentation (and any implementation that follows it) classifies the item as “no claim made,” whereas the intended orphan-wait behavior is that the growing output is a live claim. That can cause lane summaries to hide progress from a live background writer and can make coordinators treat the item as making no claim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:33

chunk_findings.detail: The added filing guidance tells agents to “read each back (`ddflow verify-filed <ids>`)” with no expected phase, needs, or wave tag. Given `ddflow task add T1 --phase wrong-phase --new` where T1 also lacks the required `wave:N` (or `no-deps`) tag, the agent can run `ddflow verify-filed T1`, get `OK`, and report the task as verified, even though the task violates the rule that every task names its phase, dependencies, and wave tag. The brief should require the expectation check to include phase/needs/wave, not only ids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/agent_brief.md:53 [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: The new driver guidance says a stopped lane containing a background-work phrase is shown as “no claim made” “unless a live pid is recorded,” but the stated orphan-wait contract also treats a growing output file as a live claim signal. Given a lane whose final summary contains “waiting on background work,” with no recorded live pid but with an output file that has grown since the last check, the documented behavior says `ddflow lanes` should still say no claim, while the intended acceptance says that growing-output evidence should make it a claim. This can cause agents or users to omit the growing-output signal or misread `lanes` output.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md:275

chunk_findings.detail: `test_wrong_needs_and_tag_are_wrong_with_both_values` verifies the `WRONG` status and the `needs`/`tags` mismatch values, but it never asserts the command's exit code. If `verify_filed` is changed so that `WRONG` records no longer force a failing exit (for example, exit code only considers `MISSING` records), this test still passes with a manifest where `T3` is expected to need `["T1"]` and tag `["wave:9"]` while the state has `T3` needing `["T1", "T2"]` and tagged `wave:3`. That violates the acceptance requirement that some wrong records exit 1.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_verify_filed.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: Given a manifest file that exists and parses successfully but contains no expectation records (for example, an empty TOML/JSON manifest), `verify_filed` returns exit 0. The argument check only sees that `manifest` is a non-empty string, `VF.load` can return an empty expectation list, `VF.check` then produces a vacuously all-OK verdict, and `res.all_ok` is true, so the function returns `O.ok`. The documented exit vocabulary says exit 2 when “nothing was asked,” and an empty manifest asks nothing; the API does not guard `if not exps` after loading.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/verify_filed.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: The `filed_max_records` knob documents that a manifest longer than the configured cap is refused with exit 3, but the stated contract for this change is that a `verify-filed` run that cannot be performed exits 2. For example, with the default cap of 500 and a manifest containing 501 records, a caller following the intended exit-code contract expects exit 2 for “could not run”; this documented exit 3 either violates that contract or makes the knob documentation wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/verify.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: The `no_claim_phrases` knob documents that a stopped lane is shown as `no claim made` unless the live-run registry holds a live pid for its item, but the change’s intent and the linked orphan-wait behavior say a growing output file also establishes a claim. For a lane whose summary says “background still running”, with no live pid but a growing output file, this documented rule says it should still be shown as `no claim made`, while the feature should treat the growing output file as evidence that work is still running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/verify.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance says a stopped lane that claims background work is running should be treated as having made a claim if either a live pid or a growing output file is recorded, but `with_no_claim` only suppresses the “no claim made” message when `probe(lane.item)` returns true, and the docstring explicitly says a growing output file is not probed. Given a stopped lane whose session summary says “running in background” and whose item has a recorded growing output file but no live pid, `probe` returns false, so the code sets `claim` to `no claim made: ... but no live process is recorded ...`, which is wrong for the required growing-output-file case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: When the expectation names a non-work kind, `check` only looks in that kind’s own table via `_check_other`; it does not apply the cross-kind wrong-kind fallback used for work-item expectations. Given a state where `st.items = {}`, `st.bugs = {}`, and `st.lessons = {"X": ...}`, and the expectation `{"id": "X", "kind": "bug"}`, `_check_other` finds no `X` in `st.bugs` and returns `MISSING`, not `WRONG` with `Mismatch("kind", "bug", "lesson")`. The module’s own work-item branch treats an id present in another table as a kind mismatch, and the docstring says a record of another kind than expected is WRONG with expected/found, so this misnames the gap and can make a coordinator believe the bug was never filed when a lesson with that id exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: `_call` does not implement the documented comma-separated `ids` form. The `ids` Param help says ids may be “comma separated in one string, or a list”, but line 18 wraps a string in a list (`[ids]`) and passes a CLI list through unchanged. Thus `ddflow verify-filed t1,t2` (one positional token) or an MCP call with `ids="t1,t2"` reaches `verify_filed` as `["t1,t2"]`, so the check treats the whole string as one id; a report that filed `t1` and `t2` is not verified correctly (it can report a bogus MISSING and exit 1, and the record count is wrong).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/verify_filed.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: The added driver text states an agent that stops waiting on background work made no claim “unless a live pid is recorded”, but the intended behavior (and the orphan-wait tie) also counts a growing output file as a live claim. An agent with a growing output file but no live pid will follow this doc and conclude no claim was made even though `ddflow lanes` is supposed to show a claim, causing the coordinator to ignore real background filing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md:270

chunk_findings.detail: The help text says the end-of-run report and `ddflow complete` “do not yet quote this output; quote it by hand until that follow-up lands.” The stated intent requires the coordinator driver doc, the agent end-of-run report (`DX-agent-final-report-rounds`), and `ddflow complete` for filing work to quote the check. Given a filing task where a background script failed to write an expected id, `ddflow complete` can still complete and report “filed” without running or quoting the state-backed `verify-filed` output, so the falsifier (“a missing id reported OK”) can still pass end-to-end despite this change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:47

chunk_findings.detail: The no-claim rule is documented as “unless the live-run registry holds a live pid for its item,” but the intent says a claim is made unless a live pid **or growing output file** is recorded. Given an agent that stops with background work whose output file is still growing but has no recorded live pid, this documentation (and any implementation that follows it) classifies the item as “no claim made,” whereas the intended orphan-wait behavior is that the growing output is a live claim. That can cause lane summaries to hide progress from a live background writer and can make coordinators treat the item as making no claim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:33

chunk_findings.detail: The added filing guidance tells agents to “read each back (`ddflow verify-filed <ids>`)” with no expected phase, needs, or wave tag. Given `ddflow task add T1 --phase wrong-phase --new` where T1 also lacks the required `wave:N` (or `no-deps`) tag, the agent can run `ddflow verify-filed T1`, get `OK`, and report the task as verified, even though the task violates the rule that every task names its phase, dependencies, and wave tag. The brief should require the expectation check to include phase/needs/wave, not only ids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/agent_brief.md:53 [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: The new driver guidance says a stopped lane containing a background-work phrase is shown as “no claim made” “unless a live pid is recorded,” but the stated orphan-wait contract also treats a growing output file as a live claim signal. Given a lane whose final summary contains “waiting on background work,” with no recorded live pid but with an output file that has grown since the last check, the documented behavior says `ddflow lanes` should still say no claim, while the intended acceptance says that growing-output evidence should make it a claim. This can cause agents or users to omit the growing-output signal or misread `lanes` output.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md:275

chunk_findings.detail: `test_wrong_needs_and_tag_are_wrong_with_both_values` verifies the `WRONG` status and the `needs`/`tags` mismatch values, but it never asserts the command's exit code. If `verify_filed` is changed so that `WRONG` records no longer force a failing exit (for example, exit code only considers `MISSING` records), this test still passes with a manifest where `T3` is expected to need `["T1"]` and tag `["wave:9"]` while the state has `T3` needing `["T1", "T2"]` and tagged `wave:3`. That violates the acceptance requirement that some wrong records exit 1.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_verify_filed.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: The added cross-kind loop is narrower than its comment: it only searches `_OTHER_TABLES`, the non-work tables used by `_check_other`, so it still misses the work-item table used by the separate work-item branch. Given a state where the expected id exists as a work item (`st.items = {"T1": ...}`) but not in any non-work table (`st.bugs = {}`, `st.lessons = {}`), an expectation `{"id": "T1", "kind": "bug"}` reaches the expected-table miss, the loop over `_OTHER_TABLES` finds no other non-work table, and returns `MISSING`. The report claim is wrong-kind (bug expected, task found), not missing, so the output misnames the gap and can cause a coordinator to treat a wrong-kind record as simply unfilled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:197

chunk_findings.detail: The changed filing guidance tells agents to read each record back with `ddflow verify-filed <ids> --phase P --tag wave:N`, but the intent and [r-task-phase-needs-wave] require `needs` to be part of the expected record. The verifier compares only fields present in the expectation, so for a task filed with the correct phase and wave tag but with missing or incorrect `needs`, the command as written can report `OK`; the agent can then report the task verified even though it violates the rule that every task states its dependencies. The guidance should require expected needs, e.g. `--needs` or a manifest record with `needs = [...]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/agent_brief.md:53

chunk_findings.detail: `with_no_claim` only adds a `claim` when the no-claim condition is true; it never clears an existing `claim`. If it is called on a lane that already has a claim (e.g. a cached lane view, or any caller that reuses `Lane` objects from a previous `with_no_claim`/`build` call), a later call where `probe` finds a live pid, or where `cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases` is emptied, still returns the old claim. For example, passing `Lane(..., state=S.STOPPED, claim="no claim made: old")` with `probe=lambda item: True` returns a lane whose `claim` remains set, even though the docstring says a live pid means a claim is made.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: For a bug/lesson/decision/rule expectation, `_check_other` decides existence only from `rid in table`. The work-item path explicitly treats a tombstone (`it.removed`) as `MISSING`, but the other-kind path does not inspect the table entry. Given a folded state where a deleted bug remains in `st.bugs` as a removed record (the same kind of tombstone the code already handles for `st.items`), a manifest record `{"id": "b1", "kind": "bug"}` returns `Verdict("b1", OK)`. The live bug is missing, yet `Result.all_ok` is true and the caller can report success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:_check_other

chunk_findings.detail: `expectations` iterates `ids` and `tags` directly, so a bare string is treated as an iterable of characters rather than a single id or tag. Given `expectations("A1")`, the function returns expectations for ids `"A"` and `"1"`, not for `"A1"`. If the state contains live items `"A"` and `"1"`, `check` returns all `OK` and `Result.all_ok` is true even though the intended id `"A1"` is missing. The same problem occurs for `tags="wave:1"`, which becomes six one-character tag expectations.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:expectations

chunk_findings.detail: `parse` does not validate that `kind` is a string. A manifest record with `kind = ["bug"]` (valid TOML/JSON array syntax) passes parsing, then `check` executes `if kind in _OTHER_TABLES:`. Because a list is unhashable, this raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of the intended `ManifestError`/exit-2 manifest failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: The command parameter help explicitly says `ids` may be “comma separated in one string, or a list,” but `_call` never splits commas: `ids=[ids] if isinstance(ids, str) else list(ids)`. Given an MCP call with `ids="A,B"` (or a CLI call with one positional argument `"A,B"`), the command is invoked with `ids=["A,B"]`, so the state is checked for one record id containing a comma instead of two ids `A` and `B`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/verify_filed.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: The documented TOML manifest example uses a top-level `[[record]]` table array, while the same help says a JSON manifest is “an object with `defaults` and `records`” and that an unknown manifest field exits 2. A user who creates the TOML manifest exactly as shown has a top-level key `record`, not `records`. If the parser follows the documented `records` key, this manifest contains zero expected records, so `ddflow verify-filed --manifest ...` can exit 0 vacuously (“every record is OK”) even though none of the claimed ids were checked; if it treats `record` as unknown instead, the documented example itself exits 2. Either way the documented manifest format is wrong and can produce a false OK or a spurious refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:19

chunk_findings.detail: The `SEG-inflight-registry` record has a non-empty `needs` list (`needs = ["RC-tree-result-cache"]`) but carries `tags = ["wave:0", "segments"]`. Under the stated expectation formula and rule `r-task-phase-needs-wave`, a task’s wave tag must be `1 + highest wave among its needs`; with any non-negative wave on the prerequisite, the expected tag is at least `wave:1`. For example, if `RC-tree-result-cache` is filed as a task with `wave:0`, this manifest expects `SEG-inflight-registry` with `wave:0`, so a correctly filed `wave:1` record would be reported WRONG, while a filed `wave:0` record would be accepted despite violating the wave rule.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/verify-filed-manifest.toml:29-30

chunk_findings.detail: The new line `lane = replace(lane, claim="")` clears the lane’s claim **before** `_claims_background(st, lane, cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases)` is called. `_claims_background` is the probe that decides whether a stopped lane’s claim claims background work, and it receives both the lane and the configured phrases, so clearing the claim first removes the text it needs to inspect. For example, given a stopped lane with `claim="background work still running"`, `cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases=["background"]`, and no live pid/growing output, the intended result is `claim="no claim made: ..."`. With this change, `_claims_background` sees an empty claim and returns no hit, so `with_no_claim` emits `claim=""` instead of the required no-claim status. The stale-claim fix should compute `hit` from the original lane and clear only when `hit` is false (or clear after the probe), not before it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: The new wrong-kind lookup checks only table membership, so it treats a tombstoned task as a live task. Given a state where the only record with id `T1` is a removed work item (`st.items["T1"].removed is True`) and an expectation `{"id": "T1", "kind": "bug"}`, the added loop sees `T1` in the task table and returns `Verdict("T1", WRONG, (Mismatch("kind", "bug", "task"),))`. The work-item path already treats `it.removed` as `MISSING`, so the correct verdict for a deleted task is `MISSING`, not `WRONG` with `found="task"`. This misnames the gap: verify-filed reports a live wrong-kind record when the live record is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:_check_other

chunk_findings.detail: For a bug/lesson/decision/rule expectation, `_check_other` decides existence only from `rid in table`. The work-item path explicitly treats a tombstone (`it.removed`) as `MISSING`, but the other-kind path does not inspect the table entry. Given a folded state where a deleted bug remains in `st.bugs` as a removed record (the same kind of tombstone the code already handles for `st.items`), a manifest record `{"id": "b1", "kind": "bug"}` returns `Verdict("b1", OK)`. The live bug is missing, yet `Result.all_ok` is true and the caller can report success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:_check_other

chunk_findings.detail: `expectations` iterates `ids` and `tags` directly, so a bare string is treated as an iterable of characters rather than a single id or tag. Given `expectations("A1")`, the function returns expectations for ids `"A"` and `"1"`, not for `"A1"`. If the state contains live items `"A"` and `"1"`, `check` returns all `OK` and `Result.all_ok` is true even though the intended id `"A1"` is missing. The same problem occurs for `tags="wave:1"`, which becomes six one-character tag expectations.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:expectations

chunk_findings.detail: `parse` does not validate that `kind` is a string. A manifest record with `kind = ["bug"]` (valid TOML/JSON array syntax) passes parsing, then `check` executes `if kind in _OTHER_TABLES:`. Because a list is unhashable, this raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of the intended `ManifestError`/exit-2 manifest failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:check

chunk_findings.detail: The command parameter help explicitly says `ids` may be “comma separated in one string, or a list,” but `_call` never splits commas: `ids=[ids] if isinstance(ids, str) else list(ids)`. Given an MCP call with `ids="A,B"` (or a CLI call with one positional argument `"A,B"`), the command is invoked with `ids=["A,B"]`, so the state is checked for one record id containing a comma instead of two ids `A` and `B`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/verify_filed.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: The documented TOML manifest example uses a top-level `[[record]]` table array, while the same help says a JSON manifest is “an object with `defaults` and `records`” and that an unknown manifest field exits 2. A user who creates the TOML manifest exactly as shown has a top-level key `record`, not `records`. If the parser follows the documented `records` key, this manifest contains zero expected records, so `ddflow verify-filed --manifest ...` can exit 0 vacuously (“every record is OK”) even though none of the claimed ids were checked; if it treats `record` as unknown instead, the documented example itself exits 2. Either way the documented manifest format is wrong and can produce a false OK or a spurious refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/verify-filed.md:19

chunk_findings.detail: The `SEG-inflight-registry` record has a non-empty `needs` list (`needs = ["RC-tree-result-cache"]`) but carries `tags = ["wave:0", "segments"]`. Under the stated expectation formula and rule `r-task-phase-needs-wave`, a task’s wave tag must be `1 + highest wave among its needs`; with any non-negative wave on the prerequisite, the expected tag is at least `wave:1`. For example, if `RC-tree-result-cache` is filed as a task with `wave:0`, this manifest expects `SEG-inflight-registry` with `wave:0`, so a correctly filed `wave:1` record would be reported WRONG, while a filed `wave:0` record would be accepted despite violating the wave rule.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/verify-filed-manifest.toml:29-30

chunk_findings.detail: The new line `lane = replace(lane, claim="")` clears the lane’s claim **before** `_claims_background(st, lane, cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases)` is called. `_claims_background` is the probe that decides whether a stopped lane’s claim claims background work, and it receives both the lane and the configured phrases, so clearing the claim first removes the text it needs to inspect. For example, given a stopped lane with `claim="background work still running"`, `cfg.verify.no_claim_phrases=["background"]`, and no live pid/growing output, the intended result is `claim="no claim made: ..."`. With this change, `_claims_background` sees an empty claim and returns no hit, so `with_no_claim` emits `claim=""` instead of the required no-claim status. The stale-claim fix should compute `hit` from the original lane and clear only when `hit` is false (or clear after the probe), not before it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:with_no_claim

chunk_findings.detail: The new wrong-kind lookup checks only table membership, so it treats a tombstoned task as a live task. Given a state where the only record with id `T1` is a removed work item (`st.items["T1"].removed is True`) and an expectation `{"id": "T1", "kind": "bug"}`, the added loop sees `T1` in the task table and returns `Verdict("T1", WRONG, (Mismatch("kind", "bug", "task"),))`. The work-item path already treats `it.removed` as `MISSING`, so the correct verdict for a deleted task is `MISSING`, not `WRONG` with `found="task"`. This misnames the gap: verify-filed reports a live wrong-kind record when the live record is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_filed.py:_check_other
